details.label: Summary
details.text: A pair of widely spaced supercells will continue to pose a threat for very large hail and occasional severe gusts in the near term

details.label: Discussion
details.text: A reservoir of strong instability amid enhanced west-northwesterly mid-level flow and related 45-55 kt of deep-layer shear will continue to support a pair of widely spaced intense supercells across southwest ND into west-central SD. Current expectations are for these supecells to pose mainly a large to very large hail threat in the near term (up to 1.5-2.5 inches in diameter) given the presence of very steep mid-level lapse rates and strong cloud-layer shear noted on the 00Z observed sounding from UNR. These cells should continue tracking southeastward, with occasional severe downdraft gusts also possible given the ample MUCAPE present. The potential for upscale growth into a bowing cluster with this ongoing activity remains highly uncertain, as stronger low-level flow and warm/moist advection related to a gradually strengthening low-level jet will tend to focus to the south/east of this region (NE into IA)

details.label: Most probable threats
details.text: MOST PROBABLE PEAK TORNADO INTENSITY...UP TO 90 MPH · MOST PROBABLE PEAK WIND GUST...55-70 MPH · MOST PROBABLE PEAK HAIL SIZE...1.50-2.50 IN
